title: A Highly Magnified Gravitationally Lensed Red QSO at z = 2.5 with a Significant Flux Ratio Anomaly
question: What is the nature of the gravitationally lensed dust-reddened QSO W2M J1042+1641 at z = 2.517, what causes its extreme flux ratio anomaly, and what are its intrinsic black hole and host galaxy properties?

recipe.goal: Measure ALMA sub-mm and JVLA radio positions and flux densities of lensed QSO images
recipe.method: Image continuum visibilities and fit 2D Gaussian / PSF profiles to each lensed QSO component using CASA imfit; predict radio star-formation flux from ALMA sub-mm flux using the far-IR-radio correlation
assumptions: Effective dust temperature of 40 K and far-IR-radio correlation of star-forming galaxies

recipe.goal: Coupled morphological and gravitational lens mass modeling of HST WFC3/IR images
recipe.method: Iteratively fit QSO point sources, Sérsic profiles for lens G, galaxy G1, and lensed QSO host Einstein ring with hostlens, reconstruct the PSF in 30 steps, and fit shared lens mass models (SIE+gamma, free SIE+gamma, SIE+gamma+GX) with glafic; also perform exploratory pixelated source reconstruction with glee
key_parameters: 16'' x 19'' cutout, pixel scale 0.06''/pixel, circular masks of ~0.3'' radius around QSO images, PSF correction box 7 to 35 pixels over 30 steps
z_l = 0.599 for G and GX, z_s = 2.517 for source
assumptions: Circular Sérsic profile with fixed n = 4 (de Vaucouleurs) for the QSO host galaxy
Singular isothermal ellipsoid plus external shear (SIE+gamma) for lens G, plus singular isothermal sphere (SIS) for perturber GX

recipe.goal: Calculate total magnification and test microlensing, extinction, and substructure explanations for the flux ratio anomaly
recipe.method: Anchor lens model magnification predictions by intersecting the C/D model distribution with a Gaussian fit to observed F160W fluxes; evaluate differential extinction; run GPU-D microlensing simulations; model substructure perturber near image A
key_parameters: Cardelli et al. (1989) extinction curve with R_V = 3.1; accretion disk inclination i = 60 deg, PA = 90 deg, relative microlens speed ~340 km/s
assumptions: Salpeter IMF with mean stellar mass 0.3 M_sun and stellar mass fraction 0.2 in De Vaucouleurs profile for kappa_*

recipe.goal: Fit optical/NIR spectra to measure QSO reddening, UV leakage, outflow velocities, and virial black hole mass
recipe.method: Fit reddened composite QSO template and two-component power-law continuum to LBT/IRTF/Keck spectra; fit Gaussian profiles to Mg II, C IV, Ly-alpha absorption features and broad H-alpha emission; compute virial black hole mass and Eddington ratio from de-reddened, de-magnified F160W and WISE W4 luminosities
key_parameters: Power-law spectral index alpha_nu = -0.5; virial mass coefficients a = 0.774, b = 0.520, c = 2.06; magnification mu = 117; bolometric corrections BC_5100 = 9.5 and BC_W4 = 7.5
assumptions: LambdaCDM cosmology with H0 = 70 km s^-1 Mpc^-1, Omega_M = 0.30, Omega_Lambda = 0.70

recipe.goal: Derive QSO host galaxy luminosity and stellar mass
recipe.method: Convert de-magnified HST F160W host magnitude to rest-frame R-band luminosity via K-correction using mag2mag; estimate stellar mass from rest-frame u-g color (F125W - F160W) and g-band luminosity using Bell et al. (2003) mass-to-light ratios
key_parameters: Host galaxy magnification factor = 15 (from hostlens for SIE+gamma+GX model)
assumptions: Coleman et al. (1980) early-type and Sbc galaxy spectral templates for K-correction; Bell et al. (2003) color-M/L relation

score_reason: The ALMA and HST datasets are publicly archived with explicit program IDs, and the analytical equations and tabular intermediate results (astrometry, photometry, kappa/gamma, spectral fits) are thoroughly documented. However, full end-to-end reproduction of the lens modeling requires a custom unreleased wrapper around hostlens/glafic and specific ALMA imaging parameters (e.g., robust value, flagged CO channels) that are not stated.
rediscovery_reason: The ALMA continuum flux densities for the four lensed images, the HST astrometry/photometry, the glafic lens mass model parameters, and the derived black hole and host galaxy masses are all quantitative results derived from public archival data (ALMA 2019.1.00964.S and HST GO-14706).
